transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Redwood Product), Jared Lee (Redwood SE); Carlos Ruiz (Nimbus CTO), Aisha Khan (Eng Mgr), Tom Brooks (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary: quick migration/demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to Redwood API. Key concerns: PHI/data residency, function-calling parity, streaming behavior, cost/latency tradeoffs, and a pilot. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

Topics covered: parity mapping (generate/chat/embeddings/rerank), streaming and function/tool calling, dedicated vs hosted for PHI, benchmarking plan, security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC), pricing/commits for Dedicated.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Carlos: Carlos here.
[00:06] Aisha: Aisha, hi.
[00:07] Tom: Tom here.
[00:08] Priya: Priya for security.
[00:10] Maya: great, from Redwood we have Ethan and Laura and Jared, Ethan's going to walk through the parity mapping then we'll do a live demo.
[00:18] Ethan: cool, hi all. so the goal today is pragmatic - we want to show how requests you have today to OpenAI/Anthropic/Together translate 1:1 to Redwood API endpoints and what differences to watch for. I'll flag places where runtime behavior differs, e.g., streaming chunk sizes, function-calling semantics, and tokenization/cost implications.
[00:36] Tom: quick note, our main workloads are chat assist (sensitive clinical notes but de-identified), embeddings for semantic search, and a small reranker for triage. latency target is <200ms p50 for short chat requests and embeddings in under 250ms p95 (rough numbers).
[00:51] Ethan: ok that's helpful. on the chat side, we support a chat.generate endpoint that conceptually maps to OpenAI chat/completions and Anthropic's chat. For parameters: messages -> messages, temperature, top_p map directly. One difference: Redwood has explicit route-level model fallbacks and can route to quantized variants for cost savings.
[01:12] Aisha: and function calling? we rely on that for structured outputs to downstream pipelines.
[01:16] Ethan: yes, function/tool calling is supported; payload is similar but small differences - e.g., Anthropic-style 'tools' name vs OpenAI 'functions' key; Redwood accepts both styles and normalizes server-side, but for best parity we'll provide a small shim/snippet in the parity matrix. sometimes the names get swapped in generated text, congruence issues, but we handle the wire format.
[01:40] Jared: also worth mentioning streaming: we stream token deltas using SSE/HTTP2. Some customers notice chunking patterns differ from OpenAI; that's usually a runtime buffer tradeoff. We'll include recommended client-side buffering knobs.
[01:54] Carlos: for embeddings, we use them for search and similarity - any vector dims differences?
[01:58] Ethan: we expose curated open models with stable dims. We'll map your Together/Anthropic dims to the closest Redwood models in the parity sheet. For exact parity we might recommend a retrain/embedding migration step, but often semantic similarity holds across comparable dims.
[02:15] Tom: cost - how do we estimate token math? our finance team wants predictable unit economics.
[02:19] Maya: good q. we show cost per token and per-embedding units; for Dedicated we do commit pricing. Ethan will run a small cost estimate given your historic usage once you share sample logs.
[02:31] Priya: security - we need SOC2, KMS, VPC options, and explicit no-logs for PHI in pilot. We also need RBAC and audit logging.
[02:40] Laura: all supported - SOC2 pack, KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS, HSM options for Private), VPC peering for Private and Dedicated. Audit logs with token-level traces are available in Console. For PHI we usually recommend Dedicated or Private deployment with customer-managed keys.
[02:58] Priya: do you support data residency in EU?
[03:00] Laura: yes, we have regions in EU and can pin deployments. We'll surface the region selection in the console and in the API.
[03:08] Carlos: show us an example of a mapping - e.g., our current OpenAI chat call vs Redwood?
[03:11] Ethan: sure, i'll share my screen - (screen share starts) - on the left is a typical OpenAI request, messages array, model: gpt-4o-mini, temperature: 0.2, function call: auto. On the right, Redwood chat.generate example: model: redwood-gpt-4o-mini-compatible, messages: same structure, temperature same. The main diff is some header names and the 'route' param if you want to pin to region/dedicated pool. Also we add an explicit 'fallback' field for automatic downgrade to quantized variants.
[03:45] Tom: does response shape change? we have downstream parsers that expect function_call.name and arguments.
[03:50] Ethan: by default we keep function_call.name/arguments shape identical. Internally we normalize Anthropic 'tools' to that shape. Wherever there is a slight variant, the parity sheet will include a snippet.
[04:05] Aisha: and streaming - will our client code break? we use streaming to render in UI.
[04:09] Ethan: streaming events look like: event: token, data: {delta:"..."} similar to OpenAI SSE. In practice chunk boundaries differ but we've got a sample client lib that handles reassembly. We'll include the JS/Python snippet.
[04:24] Carlos: performance - how do Dedicated vs Hosted compare for our p50 target?
[04:28] Jared: Dedicated gives predictable GPUs and tail latency control; Hosted is multi-tenant but we offer SLA-backed tiers. For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private; Dedicated will reduce variability, especially for smaller seq lengths. We'll propose a pilot on Hosted first to validate fidelity then move to Dedicated if latency/cost constraints require it.
[04:47] Tom: about KV cache / context windows - we use long contexts for some recall workflows. Does Redwood support long-context LLMs and KV caching?
[04:55] Ethan: yes - runtime supports KV cache management and models up to 128k tokens (model dependent). We also expose prefix caching and chunked retrieval to optimize repeated prefixes. For migration, if you're using embeddings + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the embed dimensions and tokenizer differences are the bigger migration tasks.
[05:15] Aisha: what's the friction to flip our production? we want a canary.
[05:18] Maya: we typically recommend a canary route: 5% traffic to Redwood for feature parity checks, synthetic checks for diffs in outputs, and shadow traffic for perf. Our Console supports rollout policies (canary, A/B, automatic rollback).
[05:33] Priya: any third-party certifications? also penetration tests?
[05:36] Laura: SOC2 Type II in our pack, ISO we are working on, and we provide a third-party pentest report on request. We'll share an NDA-protected security bundle.
[05:47] Carlos: ok, show me a concrete parity example for embeddings - our pipeline expects vector length 1536 from Together.
[05:52] Ethan: on Together model mapping, we have a Redwood-1536-compatible model which produces 1536-dim vectors. We'll provide conversion notes and difference metrics (cosine similarity over sample set). If exact numeric match is required you need to retrain; but for search often keep same dim and it's fine.
[06:12] Tom: reranker flow - we currently use logits-based scores from Anthropic.
[06:15] Ethan: we support raw logits in debug mode and normalized scores in the API. For reranking parity we'll add an option to return raw model scores in the response, flagged in the parity sheet.
[06:28] Aisha: cost modeling follow-up - finance will need a 6-month run rate.
[06:31] Maya: I'll share a templated consumption CSV you can plug numbers into; we'll also provide example pricing tiers for Hosted vs Dedicated.
[06:40] Carlos: any gotchas re: rate limits or quota mapping? we have bursty traffic at EOD.
[06:45] Jared: we have per-account and per-route rate limits; for Dedicated there's headroom and autoscale policies you can configure. We'll include recommended policies.
[06:55] Tom: demo time?
[06:56] Ethan: live demo - i'll run a sample chat, a function call that returns JSON, then an embedding call and a rerank.
[07:02] [07:02] Ethan: (typing) ok sending chat request... (slight pause) response streaming - you can see tokens produce as we stream. The function call example: request asks for patient_summary tool, response returns function_call with arguments containing JSON of summary sections.
[07:22] Tom: looks good. the JSON keys match our downstream parser.
[07:25] Ethan: great. embedding call now - returning 1536-d vector, here's cosine similarity example using a sample query.
[07:40] Aisha: latency for that was approx?
[07:42] Ethan: that run in our hosted EU region was ~180ms p50 for that input size. We'll run dedicated bench with your logs to confirm.
[07:51] Priya: do you log any raw prompt content? for PHI we require strict controls.
[07:55] Laura: we can disable prompt logging at ingest for Dedicated/Private and use client-side redaction or tokenization hooks; KMS will handle encryption at rest.
[08:05] Carlos: what's the proposed pilot shape?
[08:07] Maya: pilot: 2-week Hosted pilot with a small dataset, run parity tests (functional + perf) and a security review. If passes, move to Dedicated with a 3-month commit to reach production SLAs.
[08:18] Carlos: timeline - we want to be production in Q1.
[08:20] Maya: feasible; pilot this month, bench + security in 2 weeks, Dedicated onboarding in December, prod Q1 is reasonable.
[08:29] Tom: ok final questions... (none)
[08:33] Maya: recap / next steps: Ethan to deliver parity matrix + snippets by 11/15; Maya to send pilot contract + pricing by 11/14; Tom will share sample logs by 11/16; Priya to send security constraints by 11/14. We'll schedule bench run for 11/18.
[08:55] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:58] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
[09:00] Meeting ended.
